latest_release.name: v0.20.1
latest_release.body:
This release focuses on making the topology easier to read — switch rings now draw as actual loops, links are coloured by speed, and you can trace a path hop by hop. Issues also got smarter about surfacing scans and daemons that need attention.

## New Features

- Draw rings of switches as loops in the Layer 2 view, with ports and spurs arranged so ring links no longer cross each other.
- Colour links by speed in both the Layer 2 and simplified views, and show physical links on simplified maps so you can see the real cabling at a glance.
- Trace a path link by link from the edge inspector to follow traffic across your network.
- Surface failed scans and silent daemons as Issues, and export any Issues list to CSV.
- Edit subnet ranges and VLAN links by hand, and record what each new subnet is for when you create it.
- Add a Water Utility demo site built on two fiber rings, showing off the new ring layout with realistic port-to-port links.

## Improvements

- Add a Display toggle that controls whether container names appear when you zoom out, keeping whatever you have selected in full detail.
- Speed up the first draw of large topologies and stop the topology list from reloading every time you switch sites.
- Ask what brings you to Scanopy during signup and recommend a plan based on your answer.
- Scan a daemon's own networks alongside any routed scan targets, and kick off the scan straight from Create and scan.
- Offer to merge duplicate hosts when LLDP neighbours are ambiguous, and absorb inferred duplicates automatically.
- Add guided troubleshooting for an individual daemon's connection, including detection of daemons running inside WSL2.
- Link out to the relevant documentation from warnings, the setup wizard and Issues.
- Rename unmatched ports to Unclaimed and tighten vendor matching so fewer devices are mislabelled.

## Bug Fixes

- Fix the topology failing to load when its tab is opened after the page has already settled.
- Keep the viewport steady when selecting a node opens the details panel.
- Close open popovers when you click on the topology canvas.
- Ignore 0.0.0.0/0 interface subnets so they no longer appear as scan targets.
- Require and default a site in the daemon wizard, preventing daemons from being created without one.
- Keep the loading bar visible while a scan re-run is pending.

detail.readme:
# Scanopy

**Never maintain another network diagram.** Scanopy scans your network on a schedule and draws it as four views: L2, L3, workloads and applications. ![Scanopy topology view](./media/hero.png) ```bash curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scanopy/scanopy/refs/heads/main/docker-compose.yml docker compose up -d ``` Open `http://:60072` and create your account. The first discovery starts on its own. Prefer a hosted version? Try **[Scanopy Cloud](https://scanopy.net/pricing?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=cloud_trial)**. Full setup options are in the **[docs](https://scanopy.net/docs?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=docs)**. ![Github Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/scanopy/scanopy?style=for-the-badge&logo=github) ![GitHub release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/scanopy/scanopy?style=for-the-badge) ![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/scanopy/scanopy?style=for-the-badge)
![Daemon](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/scanopy/scanopy/daemon-ci.yml?label=daemon-ci&style=for-the-badge) ![Server](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/scanopy/scanopy/server-ci.yml?label=server-ci&style=for-the-badge) ![UI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/scanopy/scanopy/ui-ci.yml?label=ui-ci&style=for-the-badge)
[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1432872786828726392?logo=discord&label=discord&labelColor=white&color=7289da&style=for-the-badge)](https://discord.gg/b7ffQr8AcZ) [![Translations](https://img.shields.io/weblate/progress/scanopy?style=for-the-badge&logo=weblate)](https://hosted.weblate.org/engage/scanopy/) Scanopy replaces manual network diagrams with a continuously maintained model of what's actually running. A single daemon scans on a schedule and produces four views from each scan: L2 (physical), L3 (logical), workloads, and applications. Unlike diagrams drawn in draw.io that go stale the week they're saved, or IaC state that misses drift and resources provisioned outside the pipeline, Scanopy reflects the current state of your infrastructure. Export as SVG, Mermaid, or Confluence; embed live maps; or feed the model into your existing source of truth. > 🏢 **Running Scanopy for your business?** The [Commercial Edition](https://scanopy.net/commercial?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=self_hosted_license) adds a commercial license, more networks and seats, Confluence export, and support, all on your own infrastructure.

L2 (Physical)
Every switch, every port, every link.

L3 (Logical)
Subnets and how hosts connect across them.

Workloads
Bare metal to hypervisors to containers.

Applications
Services and their dependencies, grouped by application.
## ✨ Features **Map** - **[Network topology](https://scanopy.net/product/network-topology?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=features)**: Physical (L2) links port to port from LLDP, CDP, and switch forwarding tables, and logical (L3) topology subnet by subnet. - **[Workload mapping](https://scanopy.net/product/workload-mapping?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=features)**: VMs nested in their hypervisor, and containers inside the host that runs them. - **[Application dependency mapping](https://scanopy.net/product/application-mapping?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=features)**: Tag each server with its application once and the map fills in its services. You mark the dependencies between them. **Inventory** - **[Device inventory](https://scanopy.net/product/device-inventory?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=features)**: Every host with its IP and MAC addresses, interfaces, open ports, services, and SNMP hardware facts. Search everything with `/`, filter by site or tag, and export to CSV or read it through the REST API. - **[410+ service definitions](https://scanopy.net/services?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=features)**: Identifies databases, web servers, printers, cameras, and industrial devices (Modbus TCP, EtherNet/IP, OPC UA, BACnet) by open ports, service responses, and MAC vendor. - **[VLANs & subnets](https://scanopy.net/product/vlan-mapping?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=features)**: Reads VLAN tables from your switches over SNMP, shows native and tagged VLANs per port, and links each VLAN to its subnets. **Track & share** - **[Scan digests and snapshots](https://scanopy.net/product/snapshots?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=features)**: An email after each scheduled scan lists new, stale, and changed hosts. Snapshots record the network on a date for audits and change windows. - **[Sharing, embeds & exports](https://scanopy.net/product/sharing-and-exports?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=features)**: Read-only links with a password and expiry, live embeds in a wiki, and exports to image, document, diagram, and wiki formats. **Discovery** - **No agent per device**: A daemon on Linux, macOS, Windows, or Docker scans the networks it can reach. Deploy as many as your segments need, each on its own schedule, at the rate and subnet scope you set. - **[Integrations](https://scanopy.net/integrations?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=features)**: Docker, Aruba Instant On, Podman, Proxmox VE, UniFi Controller, Wake-on-LAN, libvirt (KVM), SNMP, SSH, and gNMI. - **Multi-user + RBAC**: Admin, member, and viewer roles, scoped per site. ## 🎯 Built for teams that manage infrastructure - **IT operations**: Network architecture and physical topology, current after every scan, across every site. - **MSPs**: Per-client documentation with read-only portals. No logins required. - **Security & compliance**: Segmentation validation and audit-ready documentation for NIS2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and CMMC. - **Platform & DevOps**: Service dependencies and workload placement without APM instrumentation. Use cases: [compliance](https://scanopy.net/solutions/compliance?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=use_cases), [multi-site networks](https://scanopy.net/solutions/multi-site-networks?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=use_cases), [shadow IT discovery](https://scanopy.net/solutions/shadow-it?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=use_cases), [plant & OT networks](https://scanopy.net/solutions/plant-ot-networks?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=use_cases), [handover & onboarding](https://scanopy.net/solutions/network-handover?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=use_cases). ## 📋 Editions and Licensing Every edition runs on your own infrastructure, so discovery data, topology and credentials stay inside your network. - **Community Edition ([AGPL-3.0](LICENSE.md)):** free and open source. AGPL-3.0 requires source disclosure for network services and copyleft compliance. - **Commercial Edition (Self-Hosted Standard, Self-Hosted Plus, Enterprise):** a commercial license for organizations that can't meet AGPL-3.0's terms or need more networks and seats. Adds Confluence export, invoice billing, procurement documents and support. Self-Hosted Plus adds multiple organizations, and Plus and Enterprise add offline license keys for air-gapped networks. **[Compare editions and get a commercial license](https://scanopy.net/commercial?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=self_hosted_license)**, or email licensing@scanopy.net. Prefer not to run it yourself? [Scanopy Cloud](https://scanopy.net/pricing?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=cloud_trial) runs the same engine as a hosted service. ## 🚀 Quick Start for Self Hosting **Docker Compose** ```bash curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scanopy/scanopy/refs/heads/main/docker-compose.yml docker compose up -d ``` **Proxmox** Use this [helper script](https://community-scripts.github.io/ProxmoxVE/scripts?id=scanopy) to create a Scanopy LXC. **Unraid** Available as an Unraid community app. --- Access the UI at `http://:60072`, create your account, and wait for the first discovery to complete. Have a commercial license? See [Installing a Self-Hosted Server](https://scanopy.net/docs/self-hosted-server/installation/?edition=commercial&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=docs). For detailed setup options and configuration, see the [Installation Guide](https://scanopy.net/docs/self-hosted-server/installation/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=docs). ## 📚 Documentation + API **[scanopy.net/docs](https://scanopy.net/docs?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=docs)** ## 🚀 Demo **[demo.scanopy.net](https://demo.scanopy.net/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=demo)**. Hosted demo app with a sample dataset. Try the full UI without installing anything. ## 🤝 Contributing We welcome contributions! See our [contributing guide](contributing.md) for details. Great first contributions: - [Adding service definitions](contributing.md#adding-service-definitions) - [Translating Scanopy](https://hosted.weblate.org/engage/scanopy/) into your language ## 💬 Community & Support - **Discord**: [Join our Discord](https://discord.gg/b7ffQr8AcZ) for help and discussions - **Issues**: [Report bugs or request features](https://github.com/scanopy/scanopy/issues/new) - **Discussions**: [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/scanopy/scanopy/discussions) --- **Translations powered by Weblate** **Built with ❤️ in NYC**
